text: The case status, the task and the timer stay rwb-case's. The readiness step reports an outcome to the parent CaseWorkflow, which moves the case status and, on the title-set outcome, raises the task to re-create the title set on the 5 working-day clock of R-SET-22. No case, task or timer table is read or written by rwb-treatment, and the message shown when a route is blocked and held is a screen text of that outcome.
why: Three of the four legacy acceptance criteria end with the case in a new state (COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED, EARLY_READINESS_CHECK) and R-SET-22 says 'raise a task', while Architecture v5 slide 41 and the connection matrix of slide 13 give the case, its CMMN state, queues, tasks and timers to rwb-case and give rwb-treatment no call to P3; DP-01 forbids reading another service's tables and no source states the blocked-route message.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11 ('own schema: state + decision record', worker and queue per service), 13 (row 'S2 Treatment': E and T to P7, E to S8, T to P5, T and E to P8, N to ACE Common, no P3 cell) and 3 (deviations pause the stage clock); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 13 (CaseWorkflow is the parent, each stage is a child, the parent forwards the event to the running stage); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-SET-22 ('Case owner | the Workbench document hub, CCMS | 5 working days'); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01 and R5.7

impact: If the parent does not raise the task, rwb-treatment must call a P3 task operation, a C dependency appears on the pair and the request element becomes a REST body; no rule or acceptance criterion changes either way.

text: The three collateral views are this service's own read-only ACE views: v_ace_collateral, v_ace_collateral_detail and v_ace_npa_asset are granted SELECT to the login of rwb-treatment, encumbrance_status, the registration state and the presence of the title document numbers are columns of that read, and no status is derived in code from lien_rank or register_date. The Land Office result arrives as the CCMS fact that ACE ingests; no live Land Office call is published. If the platform keeps the views to rwb-source-data, the read moves to that contract and a C dependency appears.
why: DP-05 allows either the contract read of rwb-source-data or the service's own views and the Work Package lists no C dependency, while the encumbrance and title statuses the rules condition on are named by no view field in the source and the architecture says the recovery.v_ace_* views are read only by rwb-source-data.
read: Context pack S2 (naming and shared platform rules: 'ACE data only through the owner's contract or v_ace_* views'; DP-05); FSD S2 v3 A2.13.2 ('ACE collateral views (v_ace_collateral, v_ace_collateral_detail; CCMS ingested by ACE), Land Office'); legacy RWB-E3-013 data table (DF-ACE-091 to DF-ACE-098, DF-ACE-196 to DF-ACE-207, DF-ACE-208 to DF-ACE-219); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DIL-02 and R-DIL-04 (encumbrance_status = clear / unresolved)

impact: If the read moves to the rwb-source-data contract, one C dependency is added to RWB-S2-E3013-APP, the view contract becomes a REST element and the encumbrance and title statuses become the contract's to fix; no criterion, rule or clock changes.

text: The readiness answer is published as an optional readiness section of the treatment answer of RWB-S2-E3001-CON at the same major version, with the properties checkType, encumbranceStatus, registrationStatus, titleSetStatus, checkedAt, ruleId, ruleVersion, holdUntil, collateralNo and assetKey. The title-set task travels as a TitleSetTaskRequest element of the stage outcome with the rule ID, the package version, the 5 working-day clock and a reason code. The names, the example values and the error mapping are the working read; no table, no column and no code list is created by them.
why: No source gives the check result a field, an element or an operation, and the legacy story lists only the treatment read, so the section and the request have to be published somewhere for four consumers to build against; the treatment read is the only published surface the officer's screen already uses.

text: The embedded Drools runtime and the DEEDINLIEU and SETTLEMENT rule packages are the service template's wave-0 capability; these two stories name the evaluated package and its version and add no build dependency of their own, because the Work Package lists none.
why: Three acceptance criteria end with the result written with its rule version and the check evaluates 37 deed-in-lieu rules and 27 settlement rules, while the Work Package's patterns are DP03, DP05, DP13 and DP19 and its H list carries no Drools contract.

text: The access guard, the outbox and inbox library and the workflow kit are service-template capabilities; the pair declares the capability area 'Treatment and offer', the right R and the call types and adds no build dependency of its own.
why: Both stories declare a capability area and a right, consume two events through an inbox and run inside a Temporal workflow, while the Work Package's H list names only the sibling contract, the decision-record contract and the gateway contract.
